lessons.evidence: CI report after the slugify fix: "✗ changelog: CHANGELOG.md: no entry under `## Unreleased` for this change". I had to add a bullet under that heading.

lessons.text: When finishing a code change in a project with a CHANGELOG.md, add the entry under `## Unreleased` in the same turn as the code fix, before reporting done, so the changelog gate does not fail afterwards.
lessons.evidence: My first turn fixed textkit/slug.py and ran the tests, but CI then failed only on the changelog; a second turn was needed just to add the entry.

lessons.text: textkit has no CI config or lint script checked in (no .github/workflows); run its tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, and say plainly that the CI changelog gate cannot be reproduced locally instead of claiming it was verified.
lessons.evidence: In the second turn I listed the repo root and found only CHANGELOG.md, tests and textkit; I had to state the changelog check itself could not be run locally.

lessons.text: This repo (the `inventory` package: inventory/stock.py, tests/test_stock.py) has a CI gate that rejects a bug-fix PR with no test whose name starts with `test_regression_`; add one alongside the fix. It has no CHANGELOG.md, so the textkit changelog rule does not apply here.

lessons.text: The `shapes` package repo (shapes/square.py, shapes/circle.py) has a CI gate `license-header` requiring `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` on line 1 of each file it checks (only files touched by the change are flagged). Pre-existing `shapes/square.py` has no header, so copying that file's style leaves it off — new files still need it. No CHANGELOG.md and no tests.
lessons.evidence: CI reported `✗ license-header: shapes/circle.py:1: missing # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` right after I followed square.py's style; a second turn added the line. `head -3 shapes/square.py` shows it still has no header, so the existing-file style was the misleading cue.

lessons.text: In a repo with no CI config checked in (gates only surface in the CI report), do a preflight in the same turn as the change: check for CHANGELOG.md and add an Unreleased bullet if present, add or update a test only when a tests/ dir already exists, put `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` on line 1 of every new Python file, give every new public function and the module a docstring, report runtime warnings with a module logger (`logging.getLogger(__name__)`), and run any installed linter named by the gate; end the final report with a line `Risk: low|medium|high` because a `release-bot` gate may require it.
lessons.evidence: In app_error I deliberately added no test file (no tests/ dir existed) and CI came back "✓ tests", so creating a tests/ dir is not a required preflight in every no-CI repo; the inventory case (#3) already had tests/test_stock.py and a named regression gate.

lessons.text: The `loader` package repo (loader/config.py) has a CI lint gate L001: library code must not use print or warnings.warn — it requires a module logger. It has no CHANGELOG.md, no tests/ dir and no CI config checked in.
lessons.evidence: My first turn implemented the missing-config-file notice with warnings.warn and CI came back "✗ lint: loader/config.py: library code must not print/warnings.warn (L001: module logger required)"; a second turn added logging.getLogger(__name__) and logger.warning. `ls -a` showed only loader/__init__.py and loader/config.py, with no tests, CHANGELOG or .github.

lessons.text: To smoke-test a package ad hoc, run python3 from the project directory: the shell tool's cwd is already the project root, so put the check script in /tmp and set PYTHONPATH to the absolute project path (from `pwd`) instead of cd'ing elsewhere and guessing.
lessons.evidence: In both turns this session I cd'd to /tmp/cfgcheck and used $OLDPWD / a guessed PYTHONPATH, and got ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'loader' twice before running `pwd` and finding the project at /tmp/expA/runs/learn-gated/r3/logging.

lessons.text: The `greet` package repo (greet/hello.py) has a CI gate `release-bot` that rejects the change unless the agent's final report ends with a line `Risk: low|medium|high`. It has no CHANGELOG.md, no tests/ dir and no CI config checked in.
lessons.evidence: CI report on this repo's change said: "✗ release-bot: final report has no `Risk: low|medium|high` line at the end", after the code change and test passed.

lessons.text: The `billing` repo (billing/tax.py, billing/settings.py, tests/test_tax.py) has only a `tests` CI gate, run as `APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; it has no CHANGELOG.md, no .github, and no regression-name/license-header/release-bot gate. billing/settings.py validates APP_ENV at import time, so an unset APP_ENV breaks test collection before any assertion runs.
lessons.evidence: CI report for this change was just "✓ tests (APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .)" with no other gates, while my local `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` first failed with "RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None" raised from billing/settings.py:5 during test module import.

lessons.text: When a failing suite reports an import/collection error, fix only that and rerun before concluding: the import error masks later assertion failures. In this billing session the import-time RuntimeError hid a wrong `tax()` result, so read the code under test for further bugs, then verify each fix with its own run (env var unset, and set to the value CI uses).
lessons.evidence: My first run showed only "ImportError: Failed to import test module: test_tax ... RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None"; running the suite again after fixing billing/settings.py was required to reveal that billing/tax.py returned 3.0 instead of 2.0.

lessons.text: When adding a preflight regression test for a fix, keep its assertions on the originally failing behavior only; do not encode new policy choices you made to unblock the tests (e.g. asserting an APP_ENV default of "dev") into the test, or state in the report that the test locks in that decision.
lessons.evidence: tests/test_regression.py::test_regression_settings_default_env asserted ENV == "dev", a default I picked myself to make collection work; the user never asked for that default, and the CI report showed no regression-test gate existed in this repo, so the assertion mainly froze my own call.

lessons.text: The `type_hints` repo (strings/ops.py, no tests/, no CHANGELOG.md, no CI config) has a CI gate `mypy/pydocstyle` that needs full annotations AND a docstring on every public function (D103) plus a module docstring (D100); its failure text, "reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring", appears even when the annotations are already there, so the docstring is what is usually missing.
lessons.evidence: strings/ops.py already had `def reverse_words(s: str) -> str:` and `mypy --disallow-untyped-defs` passed, yet CI said "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring"; running `pydocstyle strings/ops.py` showed D100 + D103 on shout and reverse_words, and adding docstrings made both tools exit 0.

lessons.text: When a CI gate names a linter (mypy, pydocstyle, flake8...), run that linter on the touched files in the same turn before reporting: check `which mypy pydocstyle` from the project root first, since these tools are often installed even when the repo has no config, and trust their output over guessing from the gate's wording.
lessons.evidence: In this session my first turn guessed at the type_hints gate (added annotations, SPDX header, tests) and still failed CI; only in the second turn did I run `which mypy pydocstyle` and get the real D103/D100 findings in one call — running them first would have saved the extra turn.

lessons.text: The `app_error` repo (users/validate.py, users/errors.py) has a CI gate `error-policy` that wants the project's own `users.errors.AppError` raised for invalid input, not a `False` return or a bare ValueError; it also reports a `tests` gate even though the repo has no tests/ dir, CHANGELOG.md or CI config.
lessons.evidence: CI report after my change read "✓ tests / ✓ error-policy"; users/errors.py contained an unused `class AppError(Exception)` and raising `AppError` (imported relatively) passed both gates on the first try.

lessons.text: When asked to raise an exception where code returned a value, first grep the package for existing exception classes (e.g. `rg -n "Exception|Error" <pkg>`) and raise the project's own type, not a builtin like ValueError.
lessons.evidence: In app_error I found users/errors.py with an unused `class AppError(Exception)`, used it instead of ValueError, and CI's `error-policy` gate passed with no rework; inventing ValueError would have risked a failing gate.

lessons.text: textkit has no CI config or lint script checked in (no .github/workflows); run its tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, and say plainly that the CI changelog gate cannot be reproduced locally instead of claiming it was verified.
lessons.evidence: In the second turn I listed the repo root and found only CHANGELOG.md, tests and textkit; I had to state the changelog check itself could not be run locally.

lessons.text: This repo (the `inventory` package: inventory/stock.py, tests/test_stock.py) has a CI gate that rejects a bug-fix PR with no test whose name starts with `test_regression_`; add one alongside the fix. It has no CHANGELOG.md, so the textkit changelog rule does not apply here.
lessons.evidence: After fixing Stock.remove and running the tests green, CI came back "✗ regression-tests: bug-fix PR contains no test named `test_regression_*`", so a second turn was needed just to add tests/test_stock.py::test_regression_remove_never_goes_negative.

lessons.text: The `shapes` package repo (shapes/square.py, shapes/circle.py) has a CI gate `license-header` requiring `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` on line 1 of each file it checks (only files touched by the change are flagged). Pre-existing `shapes/square.py` has no header, so copying that file's style leaves it off — new files still need it. No CHANGELOG.md and no tests.
lessons.evidence: CI reported `✗ license-header: shapes/circle.py:1: missing # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` right after I followed square.py's style; a second turn added the line. `head -3 shapes/square.py` shows it still has no header, so the existing-file style was the misleading cue.

lessons.text: In a repo with no CI config checked in (gates only surface in the CI report), do a preflight in the same turn as the change: check for CHANGELOG.md (add an Unreleased bullet), a tests/ dir (add/update a test), put `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` on line 1 of every new Python file, give every new public function and the module a docstring, report runtime warnings with a module logger (`logging.getLogger(__name__)`) rather than print/warnings.warn, run any installed linter named by the gate, and end the final report with a line `Risk: low|medium|high` because a `release-bot` gate may require it, instead of waiting for a second turn from CI.
lessons.evidence: This session's type_hints change followed the old list (SPDX header, tests, Risk line) but CI still failed with "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring" — the missing pydocstyle docstrings (D103/D100) were not on the preflight list, costing a second turn.

lessons.text: The `loader` package repo (loader/config.py) has a CI lint gate L001: library code must not use print or warnings.warn — it requires a module logger. It has no CHANGELOG.md, no tests/ dir and no CI config checked in.
lessons.evidence: My first turn implemented the missing-config-file notice with warnings.warn and CI came back "✗ lint: loader/config.py: library code must not print/warnings.warn (L001: module logger required)"; a second turn added logging.getLogger(__name__) and logger.warning. `ls -a` showed only loader/__init__.py and loader/config.py, with no tests, CHANGELOG or .github.

lessons.text: To smoke-test a package ad hoc, run python3 from the project directory: the shell tool's cwd is already the project root, so put the check script in /tmp and set PYTHONPATH to the absolute project path (from `pwd`) instead of cd'ing elsewhere and guessing.
lessons.evidence: In both turns this session I cd'd to /tmp/cfgcheck and used $OLDPWD / a guessed PYTHONPATH, and got ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'loader' twice before running `pwd` and finding the project at /tmp/expA/runs/learn-gated/r3/logging.

lessons.text: The `greet` package repo (greet/hello.py) has a CI gate `release-bot` that rejects the change unless the agent's final report ends with a line `Risk: low|medium|high`. It has no CHANGELOG.md, no tests/ dir and no CI config checked in.
lessons.evidence: CI report on this repo's change said: "✗ release-bot: final report has no `Risk: low|medium|high` line at the end", after the code change and test passed.

lessons.text: The `billing` repo (billing/tax.py, billing/settings.py, tests/test_tax.py) has only a `tests` CI gate, run as `APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; it has no CHANGELOG.md, no .github, and no regression-name/license-header/release-bot gate. billing/settings.py validates APP_ENV at import time, so an unset APP_ENV breaks test collection before any assertion runs.
lessons.evidence: CI report for this change was just "✓ tests (APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .)" with no other gates, while my local `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` first failed with "RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None" raised from billing/settings.py:5 during test module import.

lessons.text: When a failing suite reports an import/collection error, fix only that and rerun before concluding: the import error masks later assertion failures. In this billing session the import-time RuntimeError hid a wrong `tax()` result, so read the code under test for further bugs, then verify each fix with its own run (env var unset, and set to the value CI uses).
lessons.evidence: My first run showed only "ImportError: Failed to import test module: test_tax ... RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None"; running the suite again after fixing billing/settings.py was required to reveal that billing/tax.py returned 3.0 instead of 2.0.

lessons.text: When adding a preflight regression test for a fix, keep its assertions on the originally failing behavior only; do not encode new policy choices you made to unblock the tests (e.g. asserting an APP_ENV default of "dev") into the test, or state in the report that the test locks in that decision.
lessons.evidence: tests/test_regression.py::test_regression_settings_default_env asserted ENV == "dev", a default I picked myself to make collection work; the user never asked for that default, and the CI report showed no regression-test gate existed in this repo, so the assertion mainly froze my own call.

lessons.text: The `type_hints` repo (strings/ops.py, no tests/, no CHANGELOG.md, no CI config) has a CI gate `mypy/pydocstyle` that needs full annotations AND a docstring on every public function (D103) plus a module docstring (D100); its failure text, "reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring", appears even when the annotations are already there, so the docstring is what is usually missing.
lessons.evidence: strings/ops.py already had `def reverse_words(s: str) -> str:` and `mypy --disallow-untyped-defs` passed, yet CI said "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring"; running `pydocstyle strings/ops.py` showed D100 + D103 on shout and reverse_words, and adding docstrings made both tools exit 0.

lessons.text: When a CI gate names a linter (mypy, pydocstyle, flake8...), run that linter on the touched files in the same turn before reporting: check `which mypy pydocstyle` from the project root first, since these tools are often installed even when the repo has no config, and trust their output over guessing from the gate's wording.
lessons.evidence: In this session my first turn guessed at the type_hints gate (added annotations, SPDX header, tests) and still failed CI; only in the second turn did I run `which mypy pydocstyle` and get the real D103/D100 findings in one call — running them first would have saved the extra turn.

lessons.text: The `app_error` repo (users/validate.py, users/errors.py) has a CI gate `error-policy` that wants the project's own `users.errors.AppError` raised for invalid input, not a `False` return or a bare ValueError; it also reports a `tests` gate even though the repo has no tests/ dir, CHANGELOG.md or CI config.
lessons.evidence: CI report after my change read "✓ tests / ✓ error-policy"; users/errors.py contained an unused `class AppError(Exception)` and raising `AppError` (imported relatively) passed both gates on the first try.
